title: How to Give Feedback to a Freelancer (and Get Better Revisions)
h1: How to give feedback to a freelancer
description: How to review a first draft and give clear, specific feedback that a freelancer can act on, so revisions move the work forward instead of in circles.
intro: The first draft is rarely perfect, and that is normal. What happens next depends largely on your feedback. Clear, specific comments lead to a better second version; vague or scattered comments lead to guesswork, extra rounds and frustration on both sides. This article explains how to review work calmly, how to write feedback a freelancer can act on, and how to handle a draft that is far from what you expected.

faq.q: How quickly should I reply with feedback?
faq.a: Within a day or two if you can. Long silences slow the project and can affect the delivery date.

faq.q: Is it rude to ask for many changes?
faq.a: No, as long as they are within the agreed revisions and scope. Clear lists are easier to work with than many small messages.

faq.q: What if the first draft is completely wrong?
faq.a: Go back to the brief together. Explain what does not match and why, and ask how the seller understood it.

faq.q: Should I explain why I want a change?
faq.a: Yes. The reason helps the freelancer find the best solution, sometimes a better one than you suggested.

faq.q: Can I ask for changes after accepting the delivery?
faq.a: Usually that becomes a new order. Review everything before you accept.
